description: This line plot illustrates the performance of five different trajectory prediction methods—TrajICL, Head Tuning, LoRA 16, LoRA 64, and a baseline represented by the grey shaded area—measured by the minimum FDE20 (minFDE20) metric, which is plotted on the y-axis. The x-axis represents a “Ratio” parameter, ranging from 0 to 1.0 in linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The TrajICL method is shown as a blue line with circular markers, remaining relatively stable around a minFDE20 value of approximately 0.89 throughout the range. The Head Tuning method, depicted as an orange line with circular markers, starts at a high minFDE20 of about 1.30 at a ratio of 0 and decreases steadily to approximately 1.09 at a ratio of 1.0. The LoRA 16 method, shown as a red line with circular markers, begins at a minFDE20 of about 1.20 and declines to approximately 0.92. The LoRA 64 method, represented by a purple line with circular markers, starts at a minFDE20 of about 1.20 and decreases to approximately 0.91. The grey shaded area, which appears to represent a baseline or reference value, remains constant at a minFDE20 of approximately 1.00 across the entire ratio range. The green line, which is not labeled in the legend but appears to be a separate data series, starts at a minFDE20 of about 1.10 and decreases to approximately 0.80.
